title: The cube section is cubical for the induced product-group structure
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $p:G\to S$ a commutative group scheme with identity $e$, meaning that the addition, inverse and identity morphisms over $S$ satisfy the commutative group identities. Let $\mathcal L=(L,r,\tau)$ be a cubical rigidified line [def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line]. Give $G^3=G\times_SG\times_SG$ [def-pc-fibre-product] its componentwise group law. For each $I\subseteq\{1,2,3\}$ let $m_I:G^3\to G$ be the sum of the coordinates in $I$, with $m_\varnothing=e\circ p_3$, where $p_3:G^3\to S$ is the structure map. Form the cubical rigidified line on $G^3$ 
$$\mathcal D=\bigotimes_{I\subseteq\{1,2,3\}}(m_I^*\mathcal L)^{\otimes(-1)^{3-|I|}},$$
where pullback is tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback], the tensor product cube section and rigidification are the products of those of the factors, and exponent $-1$ means the dual line with inverse cube section and dual rigidification. The underlying line of $\mathcal D$ is $\Theta_3(L)$. The given section $\tau:\mathcal O_{G^3}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Theta_3(L)$ is a cubical rigidification-preserving isomorphism from the trivial line with unit rigidification and unit cube section to $\mathcal D$. In particular this asserts equality of cube sections on $(G^3)^3$, not merely an isomorphism of the underlying invertible modules.

source.place: I §2, cubical structures and their cocycle coherence (especially the definition I 2.4.5); compatibility needed before I 5.5. Local original WANTED. Agent formulation of the nine-variable cube-section interchange identity.

proof.text: Every $m_I$ is a homomorphism, since $G$ is commutative, including the zero homomorphism $m_\varnothing$. Pullback, tensor products and duals give cubical lines as follows: pull back each equality in [def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line] along the group homomorphism; multiply the equalities for tensor products; invert them for duals. Their symmetry, identity-face restrictions and four-variable cocycle are respectively the pulled-back, multiplied or inverted equalities. The tensor and composite-pullback identifications are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1),(2); dual evaluation is locally the pairing of a rank-one generator with its dual. Thus the specified $\mathcal D$ is a cubical rigidified line, and expanding its eight underlying factors gives exactly $\Theta_3(L)$.

proof.text:
Put $H=G^3$ and $T=H^3$, with universal coordinates $x_{ij}$ ($1\leq i,j\leq3$), row $i$ being the $i$th input of $H$. For subsets $R,C\subseteq\{1,2,3\}$ set $s_{R,C}=\sum_{i\in R,j\in C}x_{ij}$ and $\epsilon(B)=(-1)^{3-|B|}$. By the definition of the induced cube section, the section of $\Theta_3^H(\mathcal D)$ to be compared with $\Theta_3^H(\tau)$ is
$$u=\bigotimes_C\tau(s_{\{1\},C},s_{\{2\},C},s_{\{3\},C})^{\epsilon(C)}.$$
Applying the eight-factor construction to the isomorphism $\tau$ itself gives
$$v=\bigotimes_R\tau(s_{R,\{1\}},s_{R,\{2\}},s_{R,\{3\}})^{\epsilon(R)}.$$
The two underlying lines identify, using [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](2), with
$$Q=\bigotimes_{R,C}s_{R,C}^*L^{\epsilon(R)\epsilon(C)}.$$
This explicitly identifies the tensor factors and their signs before comparing sections.

proof.text:
Let $E=\{1,2,3\}\times\{1,2,3\}$. For each $B\subseteq E$ form $M_B=(\sum_{(i,j)\in B}x_{ij})^*L$ on $T$. These finitely many lines are invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1). By the locally-free-rank-one definition [def-sc-invertible-module], choose an open cover on which they all have frames $l_B$, using finite intersections of their trivializing covers. Set $l_\varnothing$ to the frame prescribed by $r$. On any such open $V$, for three disjoint subsets $B_1,B_2,B_3$ let $t(B_1,B_2,B_3)$ be the unit coefficient of $\tau(\sum_{B_1}x,\sum_{B_2}x,\sum_{B_3}x)$ in the frame
$$\frac{l_{B_1\cup B_2\cup B_3}l_{B_1}l_{B_2}l_{B_3}}{l_{B_1\cup B_2}l_{B_1\cup B_3}l_{B_2\cup B_3}l_\varnothing}.$$
The definition of $\tau$ makes $t$ symmetric and $1$ on empty arguments. Its cocycle pulled back along the four disjoint-block sum maps gives precisely the four-subset identity of [lem-sfb-disjoint-cubic-cocycle-integration]: the frames on the two sides have identical factors, which cancel. Apply that lemma to the commutative group $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_T)^\times$. It gives units $c_B$ with $c_\varnothing=1$; replace $l_B$ by $l'_B=c_Bl_B$. Its conclusion says exactly that every displayed disjoint-block cube section is now the unit coefficient in the new eight-factor frame.

proof.text:
For each fixed $C$, the three subsets $\{i\}\times C$ ($i=1,2,3$) are pairwise disjoint. Thus step 3 expresses its factor of $u$ as
$$\bigotimes_R(l'_{R\times C})^{\epsilon(R)}.$$
For each fixed $R$, the three subsets $R\times\{j\}$ are also pairwise disjoint, so its factor of $v$ is
$$\bigotimes_C(l'_{R\times C})^{\epsilon(C)}.$$
Consequently both $u$ and $v$ are the same frame
$$\bigotimes_{R,C}(l'_{R\times C})^{\epsilon(R)\epsilon(C)}$$
of $Q$. Empty $R$ or $C$ cause no exception, since $l'_\varnothing=l_\varnothing$ and the normalized cube sections have coefficient $1$. Reordering these finite products uses the symmetry in [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](2); in frames it is just commutativity of multiplication of units. Hence $u=v$ on each $V$. The sheaf equality axiom gives equality on $T$, proving the full nine-variable cube-section compatibility.

proof.text: At the identity of $H$, all eight maps $m_I$ take the value $e$. The induced rigidification of $\mathcal D$ is obtained by applying $r$ to each signed factor. The identity-face normalization in [def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line] therefore sends $\tau(e,e,e)$ to $1$. Hence $\tau$ preserves rigidifications. It is already an isomorphism of underlying lines because it is nowhere vanishing. The equality $v=u$ is exactly the condition in the same definition for that isomorphism to preserve cube sections. This proves every assertion without assuming properness, smoothness, connectedness or reducedness.
